extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, experimental investigators, and students of natural philosophy
extracted.subtask_description: A prescriptive method for interpreting and investigating natural phenomena by gathering ordered experimental histories, constructing tables of instances (presence, proximate absence, and degrees), and performing legitimate induction to discover forms, latent processes, and latent conformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary axioms (simple natures / forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin from what is constant, eternal, and universal in nature—the simple natures or forms; these primary axioms supply the radical operations and underlie higher transformations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operate from simple and universal elements rather than composite bodies; investigation of forms (eternal and immutable in reasoning) constitutes metaphysics. Emphasis: transfer attention from complicated to simple; apply mathematics to physics for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary axioms (latent process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discover latent processes by investigating concrete bodies as found in nature—trace the whole successive motion and uninterrupted efforts from beginnings to finished products (e.g., generation of metals, plants, animals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask what is lost, what remains, what is added, diluted, contracted, united, separated, continuous or broken off, what urges forward or impedes, what predominates or is subservient. Note that these processes often escape immediate sense-observation and involve very small efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Latent conformation (real anatomy of bodies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate the hidden texture, constitution, and arrangement in bodies (their latent conformation) before attempting to transform or endue them with new natures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One cannot successfully transform a body without complete knowledge of its nature; prefer reasoning and true induction with experiment and comparison to simple natures rather than crude separation by fire, which can superinduce false natures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish contemplative and operative branches (and their practical parallels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize two kinds of inquiry and practice: investigation of forms (metaphysics) and investigation of efficient causes/latent processes/conformations (physics); practical parallels are mechanics (to physics) and magic (to metaphysics) in the broad sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operative methods extend from observed nature to closely related subjects; higher radical operations depend on primary axioms. Use this classification to orient methodology and expectations of what can be acted upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare a complete and accurate natural and experimental history
rubrics_metrics.description: As a foundation, compile a complete, accurate, and orderly history of natural and experimental instances—do not imagine or invent but discover the acts and properties of nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Natural and experimental history must be fixed and exhibited in due order (through tables and coordinations), otherwise it will confound and distract the understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form tables and coordinations of instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize observations into structured tables so the understanding may act upon them effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct at least three types of tables (existence/presence, deviation/absence in proximity, and degrees/comparative instances) to enable proper induction and to avoid confusion from diffuse data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three ministrations for eliciting axioms: senses, memory, reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Elicit axioms from experiment by three ministrations: to the senses (collect observations), to the memory (record and organize), and to the mind or reason (induce axioms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect sensory data and record it before applying reason; the third ministration (true induction) is key, and the ministrations feed one another (the author advises to 'begin at the end, and go back again to the others').

rubrics_metrics.name: True and legitimate induction (the key of interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a disciplined, legitimate form of induction to derive axioms from ordered experimental data; induction is the central interpretive tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Induction must be supported by well-ordered tables and experiments; the text emphasizes beginning with induction ('begin at the end') and iterating between induction, sensory collection, and memory/organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of existence and presence (instances agreeing in the form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect and present all known instances that manifest the same nature (form) as a plain historical record—examples are enumerated for the form of heat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the collection 'as a mere history, and without any premature reflection or too great degree of refinement.' Use exhaustive, varied instances (the text gives a long example list for heat: sun rays, burning mirrors, flame, warm baths, vapors, friction, chemical actions, animals, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of deviation or absence in proximity (negatives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assemble proximate negative instances—cases closely related to affirmative instances where the given nature is absent—to test and delimit the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Class negatives under the affirmatives and focus on objects with close connection to those where the nature is present (examples: lunar rays not warm, middle region of air, polar reflections weakly producing heat). Use negatives to refine understanding of causal conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of degrees or comparative instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect instances showing the nature present in greater or lesser degree—compare increases and decreases within the same object or across different objects to correlate the form with measurable degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A true form should uniformly diminish and increase with the given nature. The text illustrates comparative degrees for heat (latent heat in putrefaction, warmth of animals, degrees across animal species and body parts, effects of confinement, friction, dissolution, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid crude separation by fire; prefer reasoned separation and comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Beware that separation and solution by fire (distillation, calcination) can create or superinduce natures not originally present in the compound and so may mislead about latent conformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer reasoning and true induction aided by experiment and comparison with simple natures; use chemical separations cautiously and look for fallacies introduced by heat or destructive operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek smallest, subtile efforts and continuous processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that many natural acts are produced by the smallest efforts, often too small to strike the senses; investigation must attend to subtile, continuous processes rather than only overt measures or symptoms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inquire into minute and continuous operations (what is being lost, added, diluted, contracted, united, separated, continuous vs broken off, what impels or impedes), since these underlie observable phenomena and are crucial for directing change in nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate spirits, tangible essences, and internal structure (anatomy of latent conformation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine the spirit and tangible essence of bodies (copious or meagre, aëriform or igniform, active or sluggish), their fibres, hairs, pores, passages, veins, cells, and rudiments—the real internal anatomy that governs properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comparison with similar bodies and reductions to simple natures; the author notes that true insight into latent conformation is subtle and often obscured by methods like fire, so rely on careful induction and comparative experiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply mathematics to physics; reduce complexity to simple elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfer attention from the complicated and incommensurable to the simple and commensurable; apply mathematical reasoning to physical investigation for clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not be alarmed by vast numbers or fractions; mathematical methods make inquiry into nature more plain and perspicuous (analogy to elements of letters and simple musical tones).
